Part 1 of 2

# PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES] Contents of this Part

## I COSTS PAYABLE BY OR TO PARTICULAR PERSONS

## Pre-commencement disclosure and orders for disclosure against a person who is not a party

## 46.1

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (1) This paragraph applies where a person applies –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (a) for an order under –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (i) section 33 of the Senior Courts Act 1981; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (ii) section 52 of the County Courts Act 1984,

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (which give the court powers exercisable before commencement of proceedings); or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (b) for an order under –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (i) section 34 of the Senior Courts Act 1981; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (ii) section 53 of the County Courts Act 1984,

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (which give the court power to make an order against a non-party for disclosure of documents, inspection of property etc.). [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (2) The general rule is that the court will award the person against whom the order is sought that person’s costs –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (a) of the application; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (b) of complying with any order made on the application. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (3) The court may however make a different order, having regard to all the circumstances, including –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (a) the extent to which it was reasonable for the person against whom the order was sought to oppose the application; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.1] (b) whether the parties to the application have complied with any relevant pre-action protocol. ## Costs orders in favour of or against non-parties

## 46.2

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.2] (1) Where the court is considering whether to exercise its power under section 51 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 (costs are in the discretion of the court) to make a costs order in favour of or against a person who is not a party to proceedings, that person must –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.2] (a) be added as a party to the proceedings for the purposes of costs only; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.2] (b) be given a reasonable opportunity to attend a hearing at which the court will consider the matter further. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.2] (2) This rule does not apply –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.2] (a) where the court is considering whether to –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.2] (i) make an order against the Lord Chancellor in proceedings in which the Lord Chancellor has provided legal aid to a party to the proceedings;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.2] (ii) make a wasted costs order (as defined in rule 46.8); and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.2] (b) in proceedings to which rule 46.1 applies (pre-commencement disclosure and orders for disclosure against a person who is not a party). [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.2] (3) Neither rule 19.4 nor rule 20.7 applies to the joinder of a person under paragraph (1). ## Limitations on court’s power to award costs in favour of trustee or personal representative

## 46.3

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.3] (1) This rule applies where –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.3] (a) a person is or has been a party to any proceedings in the capacity of trustee or personal representative; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.3] (b) rule 44.5 does not apply. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.3] (2) The general rule is that that person is entitled to be paid the costs of those proceedings, insofar as they are not recovered from or paid by any other person, out of the relevant trust fund or estate. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.3] (3) Where that person is entitled to be paid any of those costs out of the fund or estate, those costs will be assessed on the indemnity basis. ## Costs where money is payable by or to a child or protected party

## 46.4

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (1) This rule applies to any proceedings where a party is a child or protected party and –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (a) money is ordered or agreed to be paid to, or for the benefit of, that party; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (b) money is ordered to be paid by that party or on that party’s behalf. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (‘Child’ and ‘protected party’ have the same meaning as in rule 21.1(2).)

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (2) The general rule is that –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (a) the court must order a detailed assessment of the costs payable by, or out of money belonging to, any party who is a child or protected party; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (b) on an assessment under paragraph (a), the court must also assess any costs payable to that party in the proceedings, unless –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (i) the court has issued a default costs certificate in relation to those costs under rule 47.11; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (ii) the costs are payable in proceedings to which Section IV of Part 45 applies. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (3) The court need not order detailed assessment of costs in the circumstances set out in paragraph (5) or in Practice Direction 46. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (4) Where –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (a) a claimant is a child or protected party; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (b) a detailed assessment has taken place under paragraph (2)(a),

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] the only amount payable by the child or protected party is the amount which the court certifies as payable. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (5) Where the costs payable comprise only the success fee claimed by the child’s or protected party’s legal representative under a conditional fee agreement or the balance of any payment under a damages based agreement, the court may direct that—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (a) the assessment procedure referred to in rule 46.10 and paragraph 6 of Practice Direction 46 shall not apply; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (b) such costs be assessed summarily. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.4] (This rule applies to a counterclaim by or on behalf of a child or protected party by virtue of rule 20.3.)

## Litigants in person

## 46.5

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (1) This rule applies where the court orders (whether by summary assessment or detailed assessment) that the costs of a litigant in person are to be paid by any other person. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (2) The costs allowed under this rule will not exceed, except in the case of a disbursement, two-thirds of the amount which would have been allowed if the litigant in person had been represented by a legal representative. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (3) The litigant in person shall be allowed –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (a) costs for the same categories of –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (i) work; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (ii) disbursements,

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] which would have been allowed if the work had been done or the disbursements had been made by a legal representative on the litigant in person’s behalf;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (b) the payments reasonably made by the litigant in person for legal services relating to the conduct of the proceedings; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (c) the costs of obtaining expert assistance in assessing the costs claim. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (4) The amount of costs to be allowed to the litigant in person for any item of work claimed will be –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (a) where the litigant can prove financial loss, the amount that the litigant can prove to have been lost for time reasonably spent on doing the work; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (b) where the litigant cannot prove financial loss, an amount for the time reasonably spent on doing the work at the rate set out in Practice Direction 46. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (5) A litigant who is allowed costs for attending at court to conduct the case is not entitled to a witness allowance in respect of such attendance in addition to those costs. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (6) For the purposes of this rule, a litigant in person includes –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (a) a company or other corporation which is acting without a legal representative; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (b) any of the following who acts in person (except where any such person is represented by a firm in which that person is a partner) –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (i) a barrister;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (ii) a solicitor;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (iii) a solicitor’s employee;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (iv) a manager of a body recognised under section 9 of the Administration of Justice Act 1985 1 ; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.5] (v) a person who, for the purposes of the 2007 Act 2 , is an authorised person in relation to an activity which constitutes the conduct of litigation (within the meaning of that Act). ## Costs where the court has made a group litigation order

## 46.6

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (1) This rule applies where the court has made a Group Litigation Order (‘GLO’). [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (2) In this rule –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] ‘individual costs’ means costs incurred in relation to an individual claim on the group register;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] ‘common costs’ means –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (i) costs incurred in relation to the GLO issues;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (ii) individual costs incurred in a claim while it is proceeding as a test claim, and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (iii) costs incurred by the lead legal representative in administering the group litigation; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] ‘group litigant’ means a claimant or defendant, as the case may be, whose claim is entered on the group register. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (3) Unless the court orders otherwise, any order for common costs against group litigants imposes on each group litigant several liability for an equal proportion of those common costs. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (4) The general rule is that a group litigant who is the paying party will, in addition to any liability to pay the receiving party, be liable for –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (a)the individual costs of that group litigant’s claim; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (b)an equal proportion, together with all the other group litigants, of the common costs. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (5) Where the court makes an order about costs in relation to any application or hearing which involved –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (a) one or more GLO issues; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (b) issues relevant only to individual claims,

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] the court will direct the proportion of the costs that is to relate to common costs and the proportion that is to relate to individual costs. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (6) Where common costs have been incurred before a claim is entered on the group register, the court may order the group litigant to be liable for a proportion of those costs. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (7) Where a claim is removed from the group register, the court may make an order for costs in that claim which includes a proportion of the common costs incurred up to the date on which the claim is removed from the group register. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.6] (Part 19 sets out rules about group litigation.)

## Orders in respect of pro bono representation

## 46.7

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (1) Where the court makes an order under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (a) the court may order the payment to the prescribed charity of a sum no greater than the costs specified in Part 45 to which the party with pro bono representation would have been entitled in accordance with that Part and in respect of that representation had it not been provided free of charge; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (b) where Part 45 does not apply, the court may assess the amount of the payment (other than a sum equivalent to fixed costs) to be made by the paying party to the prescribed charity by –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (i) conducting a summary assessment; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (ii) making an order for and conducting a detailed assessment,

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] of a sum equivalent to all or part of the costs the paying party would have been ordered to pay to the party with pro bono representation in respect of that representation had it not been provided free of charge. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (2) Where the court makes an order under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act, the order must direct that the payment by the paying party be made to the prescribed charity. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (3) The receiving party must send a copy of the order to the prescribed charity within 7 days of receipt of the order. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (4) Where the court considers making or makes an order under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act, Parts 44 to 47 apply, where appropriate, with the following modifications –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (a) references to ‘costs orders’, ‘orders about costs’ or ‘orders for the payment of costs’ are to be read, unless otherwise stated, as if they refer to an order under section 194(3);

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (b) references to ‘costs’ are to be read as if they referred to a sum equivalent to the costs that would have been claimed by, incurred by or awarded to the party with pro bono representation in respect of that representation had it not been provided free of charge; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.7] (c) references to ‘receiving party’ are to be read, as meaning a party who has pro bono representation and who would have been entitled to be paid costs in respect of that representation had it not been provided free of charge. ## II COSTS RELATING TO LEGAL REPRESENTATIVES

## Personal liability of legal representative for costs – wasted costs orders

## 46.8

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.8] (1) This rule applies where the court is considering whether to make an order under section 51(6) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 3 (court’s power to disallow or (as the case may be) order a legal representative to meet, ‘wasted costs’). [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.8] (2) The court will give the legal representative a reasonable opportunity to make written submissions or, if the legal representative prefers, to attend a hearing before it makes such an order. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.8] (3) When the court makes a wasted costs order, it will –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.8] (a) specify the amount to be disallowed or paid; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.8] (b) direct a costs judge or a district judge to decide the amount of costs to be disallowed or paid. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.8] (4) The court may direct that notice must be given to the legal representative’s client, in such manner as the court may direct –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.8] (a) of any proceedings under this rule; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.8] (b) of any order made under it against his legal representative. ## Basis of detailed assessment of solicitor and client costs

## 46.9

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.9] (1) This rule applies to every assessment of a solicitor’s bill to a client except a bill which is to be paid out of the Community Legal Service Fund under the Legal Aid Act 1988 4 or the Access to Justice Act 1999 5 or by the Lord Chancellor under Part 1 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.9] (2) Section 74(3) of the Solicitors Act 1974 6 applies unless the solicitor and client have entered into a written agreement which expressly permits payment to the solicitor of an amount of costs greater than that which the client could have recovered from another party to the proceedings. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.9] (3) Subject to paragraph (2), costs are to be assessed on the indemnity basis but are to be presumed –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.9] (a) to have been reasonably incurred if they were incurred with the express or implied approval of the client;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.9] (b) to be reasonable in amount if their amount was expressly or impliedly approved by the client;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.9] (c) to have been unreasonably incurred if –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.9] (i) they are of an unusual nature or amount; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.9] (ii) the solicitor did not tell the client that as a result the costs might not be recovered from the other party. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.9] (4) Where the court is considering a percentage increase on the application of the client, the court will have regard to all the relevant factors as they reasonably appeared to the solicitor or counsel when the conditional fee agreement was entered into or varied. ## Assessment procedure

## 46.10

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.10] (1) This rule sets out the procedure to be followed where the court has made an order under Part III of the Solicitors Act 1974 for the assessment of costs payable to a solicitor by the solicitor’s client. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.10] (2) The solicitor must serve a breakdown of costs within 28 days of the order for costs to be assessed. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.10] (3) The client must serve points of dispute within 14 days after service on the client of the breakdown of costs. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.10] (4) The solicitor must serve any reply within 14 days of service on the solicitor of the points of dispute. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.10] (5) Either party may file a request for a hearing date –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.10] (a) after points of dispute have been served; but

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.10] (b) no later than 3 months after the date of the order for the costs to be assessed. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.10] (6) This procedure applies subject to any contrary order made by the court. ## III COSTS ON ALLOCATION AND RE-ALLOCATION

## 46.11 Omitted

## 46.12 Omitted

## Costs following allocation, re-allocation and non-allocation

## 46.13

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.13] (1) Any costs orders made before a claim is allocated will not be affected by allocation. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.13] (2) Omitted

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.13] (3) Where the court is assessing costs on the standard basis of a claim which concluded without being allocated to a track, it may restrict those costs to costs that would have been allowed on the track to which the claim would have been allocated if allocation had taken place. ## IV COSTS-ONLY PROCEEDINGS

## Costs-only proceedings

## 46.14

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (1) This rule applies where –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (a) the parties to a dispute have reached an agreement on all issues (including which party is to pay the costs) which is made or confirmed in writing; but

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (b) they have failed to agree the amount of those costs; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (c) no proceedings have been started. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (1A) This rule does not apply to a dispute to which the procedure under section 10 of Practice Direction 27B applies. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (2) Where this rule applies, the procedure set out in this rule must be followed. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (3) Proceedings under this rule are commenced by issuing a claim form in accordance with Part 8. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (4) The claim form must contain or be accompanied by the agreement or confirmation. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (5) In proceedings to which this rule applies the court may make an order for the payment of costs to be assessed and/or, where appropriate, may determine the fixed costs. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (6) Where this rule applies but the procedure set out in this rule has not been followed by a party –

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (a) that party will not be allowed costs greater than those that would have been allowed to that party had the procedure been followed; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (b) the court may award the other party the costs of the proceedings up to the point where an order for the payment of costs is made. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.14] (7) Rule 44.5 (amount of costs where costs are payable pursuant to a contract) does not apply to claims started under the procedure in this rule. ## V COSTS IN CLAIMS FOR JUDICIAL REVIEW

## Claims for judicial review: costs against interveners

## 46.15

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.15] (1) In this rule the terms “intervener” and “relevant party” have the same meaning as in section 87 of the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015 (“the 2015 Act”). [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.15] (2) A relevant party may apply to the court for an order for an intervener to pay costs in accordance with section 87 of the 2015 Act. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.15] (Section 87 of the 2015 Act applies to judicial review proceedings in the High Court and Court of Appeal.)

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.15] (Rule 54.17 makes provision for any person to be able to apply for permission to file evidence or make representations at the hearing of a judicial review.)

## Judicial review costs capping orders – general

## 46.16

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.16] (1) For the purposes of this Section—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.16] (a) “judicial review costs capping order” means a costs capping order made by the High Court or the Court of Appeal in accordance with sections 88, 89 and 90 of the 2015 Act; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.16] (b) “the 2015 Act” means the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.16] (2) This Section does not apply to a costs capping order under rule 3.19. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.16] (Rule 3.19 makes provision for orders limiting the amount of future costs (including disbursements) which a party may recover pursuant to an order for costs subsequently made.)

## Applications for judicial review costs capping orders

## 46.17

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (1) An application for a judicial review costs capping order must—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (a) be made on notice and, subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), in accordance with Part 23; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (b) be supported by evidence setting out—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (i) why a judicial review costs capping order should be made, having regard, in particular, to the matters at sub-sections (6) to (8) of section 88 of the 2015 Act and sub-section (1) of section 89 of that Act;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (ii) a summary of the applicant’s financial resources;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (iii) the costs (and disbursements) which the applicant considers the parties are likely to incur in the future conduct of the proceedings; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (iv) if the applicant is a body corporate, whether it is able to demonstrate that it is likely to have financial resources available to meet liabilities arising in connection with the proceedings. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), the applicant must serve a copy of the application notice and copies of the supporting documents on every other party. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (3) On application by the applicant, the court may dispense with the need for the applicant to serve the evidence setting out a summary of the applicant’s financial resources on one or more of the parties. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (4) The court may direct the applicant to provide additional information or evidence to support its application. ## Court to consider making directions

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > Court to consider making directions] 46.18 If the applicant is a body corporate, and the evidence supporting its application in accordance with rule 46.17(1)(b)(iv) sets out that it is unable to demonstrate that it is likely to have financial resources available to meet liabilities arising in connection with the proceedings, the court must consider giving directions for the provision of information about the applicant’s members and their ability to provide financial support for the purposes of the proceedings. ## Applications to vary judicial review costs capping orders

## 46.19

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.19] (1) An application to vary a judicial review costs capping order must be made on notice and, subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), in accordance with Part 23. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.19] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), the applicant must serve a copy of the application notice and copies of any supporting documents on every other party. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.19] (3) If the application is supported by evidence setting out a summary of the applicant’s financial resources, the court may, on application by the applicant, dispense with the need for the applicant to serve such evidence on one or more of the parties. ## VII SCALE COSTS FOR CLAIMS IN THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ENTERPRISE COURT

## Scope and interpretation

## 46.20

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), this Section applies to proceedings in the Intellectual Property Enterprise Court. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (2) This Section does not apply where—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (a)the court considers that a party has behaved in a manner which amounts to an abuse of the court’s process; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (b)the claim concerns the infringement or revocation of a patent or registered design or registered trade mark the validity of which has been certified by a court or by the Comptroller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks in earlier proceedings. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (3) The court will make a summary assessment of the costs of the party in whose favour any order for costs is made. Rules 44.2(8), 44.7(b) and Part 47 do not apply to this Section. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (4) ‘Scale costs’ means the costs set out in Table A and Table B of the Practice Direction supplementing this Part. ## Amount of scale costs

## 46.21

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (1) Subject to rule 46.22, the court will not order a party to pay total costs of more than—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (a)£60,000 on the final determination of a claim in relation to liability; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (b)£30,000 on an inquiry as to damages or account of profits. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (2) The amounts in paragraph (1) apply after the court has applied the provision on set off in accordance with rule 44.12(a). [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (3) The maximum amount of scale costs that the court will award for each stage of the claim is set out in Practice Direction 46. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (4) The amount of the scale costs awarded by the court in accordance with paragraph (3) will depend on the nature and complexity of the claim.
